newsitem.title: BOSNIA: OSCE extends deadline for Bosnia's postal vote.
newsitem.headline: OSCE extends deadline for Bosnia's postal vote.

text.p: The international organisers of Bosnia's elections extended the deadline for votes from refugees living abroad, election officials said on Thursday.

Officials from the Organisation for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE), which is responsible for supervising the national elections, said the extension was in response to organisational problems with the postal vote.
The OSCE said it would accept ballots through the post from refugees up to the voting date of September 14, the day when in-country voting is due to take place.
The OSCE has yet to explain how it will ensure refugees do not vote twice -- once through the post from their country of refuge, and a second time by travelling back to Bosnia on polling day.

The decision follows widespread complaints from refugees who said they did not receive their ballot documents through the post in time to vote and return them before the original deadline of midnight on Tuesday.
Election monitors said it was too early to say how many refugees had experienced problems with their ballot papers.

Although there are some two million Bosnian refugees scattered across the globe, about 641,000 registered to cast postal ballots. The rest will must travel to Bosnia to vote in person on September 14 if they wish to participate.
Most refugees are in the neighbouring states of Rump Yugoslavia and Croatia, as well as in Germany.

The extension follows an earlier decision to postpone the poll for municipal assemblies to give the OSCE time to address voter registration irregularities that could have skewed the results in favour of the Bosnian Serbs in key towns.

Independent human rights groups have criticised the OSCE for pushing ahead with the elections under Western pressure, despite evidence that the vote is unlikely to be "free and fair" as the Dayton peace treaty requires.
